additions.reason: The text uses explicit bechina language: 'מֶלֶךְ בְּמִשְׁפָּט יַעֲמִיד אָרֶץ. בְּמִשְׁפָּט דַּיְקָא' — the verse 'a king establishes the land through justice' is read as the definition of what mishpat/poskim accomplish. 'נַעֲשֶׂה מֶלֶךְ וּמוֹשֵׁל' — one BECOMES a king and ruler through Torah law. The royalty/dominion is a bechina of the power of mishpetei haTorah. However, care is needed: this could also be eitza (Torah law PRODUCES the status of king). The text uses 'נַעֲשֶׂה' (becomes), suggesting a transformation/result — leaning toward eitza rather than bechina. Flagged for review; tentatively assigned to Package 1 domain context but noted as possibly eitza.
